topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's objectives, reviewing the progression of cancer mutations and framing the discussion around Hanahan and Weinberg's hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulation of Proliferative and Growth-Inhibitory Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades confer self-sufficiency in growth signals and insensitivity to growth-inhibitory cues.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells arrest in an immature proliferative state instead of completing terminal lineage differentiation, using hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma as models.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis and Cellular Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome intrinsic anti-oncogenic fail-safes by disrupting apoptotic machinery, maintaining telomere length, and bypassing p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Reprogramming of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex phenotypic hallmarks and examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways through aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite-driven epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how growing tumors overcome diffusion limits by inducing new blood vessel formation through an imbalance of angiogenic activators and inhibitors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Progression of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multistep metastatic cascade, examining how cancer cells invade, survive circulation, and colonize distant organs despite significant mechanical and biological inefficiencies.

topics.label: Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the convergence of cancer hallmarks across diverse mutational paths, highlighting recent conceptual literature, and inviting student questions.
